quotes.text: Learn how to accept credit card payments using installments across a variety of Stripe products.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Installments only works with `payment` mode, not `setup` or `subscription` mode.
If you use dynamic payment methods, don’t set `payment_method_options[card][installments][enabled]`.
You must explicitly unset `payment_method_options[card][installments][plan]` when confirming the PaymentIntent again to indicate the absence of an installment plan.
You can enable installments for individual invoices but not for subscriptions.

findings: The complete 2026-11-07 canonical capture is only a variant index: it names Checkout, Elements, Direct API, Invoices and No code/Payment Links routes, with no parameters, eligibility, plans, test cards or payment outcomes (new raw lines 5-17). The 763-line older 2026-05-01 capture contains the substantive instructions for all five (old raw lines 8-763). The 768-line diff is replacement by navigation, not a demonstrated product change (diff lines 1-768).

The older Checkout variant uses payment mode only. With dynamic payment methods, installments appear automatically and the card.installments.enabled field must be omitted; without dynamic methods, the Checkout Session example explicitly sets enabled:true (old raw lines 28-55). The Payment Element variant has the same split for its PaymentIntent example (old raw lines 82-106), then returns a client secret and calls confirmPayment with return_url; issuer declines can occur (old raw lines 104-116). Session URL navigation is not payment success.

The older Direct API sequence collects card details client-side through Stripe.js/Elements, creates an unconfirmed server-side PaymentIntent with a PaymentMethod ID, returns available_plans, lets the customer choose, then confirms on the server; a plan persists until explicitly unset when retrying with a different card (old raw lines 128-251, 304-487). The 2026-11-07 index merely links this variant (new raw line 15) and does not retest or renew those API and client/server details.

The older invoice variant supports individual send_invoice invoices, not charge_automatically or subscriptions; customer-configured Account and Customer identities use customer_account and customer respectively, and hosted invoice selection precedes retrieval of a selected plan from PaymentIntent (old raw lines 489-681). Older Payment Links could be toggled in Dashboard, and old sandbox card and PaymentMethod test examples include a declined Visa card (old raw lines 709-763). New raw lines 16-17 confirm only navigation to those variants.

The mapped source carries a May 2026 dated digest and old raw reference (source lines 4-7, 13-46), but its unconditional Checkout and Payment Element enabled:true summaries (source lines 17-19) conflict with the May guide's dynamic-method conditional paths (old raw lines 28-55, 82-106). This is a required baseline summary correction independent of the November navigation-only raw. Add the November raw as a navigation reference without silently redating the older detailed claims.

Related concept and index context was checked at wiki/index.md:7, wiki/stripe-index.md:231-233, wiki/concepts/stripe-jp-installments.md:10-14,50-53, wiki/concepts/stripe-installments.md:37-49 and wiki/companies/stripe.md:469-471. Japan-account, JPY, JP-issued-credit-card and no-recurring restrictions are preserved there and in the older Japan source, but are not stated by the November variant index (wiki/sources/source-stripe-jp-installments.md:13-23).

answers.Q1: The complete 2026-11-07 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/jp-installments/accept-a-payment establishes only five variant links: Checkout, Elements, Direct API, Invoices and Payment Links; new raw lines 5-17 provide no requirements, parameters or outcomes. The older full guide documents Checkout payment mode, client card collection, server PaymentIntent plan retrieval and confirmation, individual send_invoice invoices and Payment Links in old raw lines 8-763. In both Checkout and Payment Element, dynamic payment methods expose installments automatically and the enabled field must be omitted; non-dynamic examples explicitly set enabled:true (old raw lines 28-55, 82-106). source-stripe-jp-installments-accept-payment.md misstates this conditional split at lines 17-19 and needs a baseline correction. Related dated Japan concept and source restrict eligibility to Japan Stripe accounts, JP-issued credit cards, JPY and no recurring/off-session use; the November index does not reverify those restrictions. A Checkout session, available plan or invoice creation is not a successful charge.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/jp-installments/accept-a-payment, replacing a combined guide with an index is navigation and presentation, not a demonstrated removal of any payment route; compare old raw lines 14-763 with new raw lines 9-17. No new substantive raw behavior is established, but source-stripe-jp-installments-accept-payment.md has a material pre-existing conflict: lines 17-19 generalize enabled:true and warn only about false, whereas the May guide says omit the enabled field entirely with dynamic payment methods and set true in the non-dynamic Checkout Session or PaymentIntent path (old raw lines 28-55, 82-106). Correct that source, retain the May date for eligibility, mode, plan-clearing, Account/Customer and test claims, and record November only as navigation. The links do not verify current variant APIs or UI. Preserve client Stripe.js versus server secret-key boundaries and distinguish plan availability, confirmation attempt, redirect and invoice delivery from payment success.
